annotations.title: Check regular expressions for ReDoS (catastrophic backtracking)

description: Use when a regular expression will run on user input or untrusted data (form validation, request routing, log parsing, WAF or search rules) and must not hang the server, or when reviewing a codebase's regexes for ReDoS (signals: "is this regex safe", "ReDoS", "catastrophic backtracking", "regex hangs", "CPU spike on validation", "security review of regexes", "(a+)+"). Analyzes 1 to 20 patterns with recheck (automaton analysis with a fuzzing fallback) for backtracking engines with JavaScript syntax, and returns per pattern: safe (proven linear, or no attack found when backreferences or lookarounds force fuzzing), or vulnerable with the complexity (exponential, or polynomial with its degree), a concrete attack string (repr like 'a'.repeat(31) + '\\x00', plus the string itself when short), the hot part of the pattern and a fix hint. Example: {"patterns":["^(a+)+$","/^([a-z]+\\s)*$/","^[\\w.+-]+@[\\w-]+\\.[\\w.-]+$"]}. Python re, PCRE, Java, .NET and Ruby backtrack the same way on these constructs; RE2, Go regexp and Rust regex are linear-time and not affected. To also run the pattern on test strings, use sieve_test_regex.

flags.description: Flags for every pattern given as a raw source (literals keep their own). JavaScript flags d g i m s u v y.
